title: Rate envelope handoff / fallback loop triggering customer outage for Acme Analytics
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: After a scheduled rollout that changed model routing for several Dedicated pools, Acme Analytics experienced sustained 429s and degraded throughput for ~90 minutes. Support escalated at 2026-03-10T08:45Z. This ticket tracks the investigation, hotfix, and follow-up work to prevent recurrence.

Impact: Customer-facing outage affecting 1 high-revenue tenant (Acme Analytics) on both Hosted->Dedicated hybrid routing and their Private deployment mirror. Observed symptoms: burst of 429s, then a prolonged recovery where traffic was repeatedly rejected despite available capacity in adjacent pools. Root cause was a mismatch in how the proxy and the admission-controller interpret "rate envelopes" (credit/epoch semantics) during fallback routing, which produced a feedback loop: fallback routing redirected traffic into a pool that immediately hit admission limits, which in turn triggered more fallback decisions.

Repro steps observed in staging:
1) Simulate a model rollout that changes routing from hosted to dedicated pool A.
2) Induce a controlled spike (30% above steady-state QPS) with short-lived bursts.
3) Observe admission-controller mark pool A as degraded and emit fallback policy to pool B.
4) Proxy performs immediate handoff but continues to report legacy credit-epoch markers to admission-controller, leading to double-counting of outstanding in-flight credits and premature denial.

Root cause analysis (short):
- Admission-controller and proxy use different epoch anchoring for credit buckets when fallback decisions are computed.
- The fallback path lacked an explicit grace reconciliation step; admission-controller treated handoff traffic as new quota usage instead of continuing previous envelope accounting.
- This produced a transient but self-sustaining loop where fallback routing increased pressure on the secondary pool and prevented automated recovery.

Mitigation performed (on-call):
- 2026-03-10 09:05Z: Applied emergency override to fallback routing policy (temporary per-tenant bypass) for Acme which routed back to hosted pool until fix deployed.
- 2026-03-10 09:30Z: Injected 48-hour supplemental credits to Acme's account to clear backlog and allow traffic to drain.
- Monitoring: Enabled additional Grafana panels for credit-epoch alignment and admission-controller decision counts.

Fix implemented:
- admission-controller: added an explicit "handoff reconciliation" step that maps proxy epoch markers to controller epoch buckets before counting usage. This prevents double-counting during handoff.
- proxy: added idempotent handoff acknowledgement so the controller can observe a completed handoff instead of re-issuing fallback decisions.
- added unit tests covering epoch drift scenarios and an end-to-end test in staging exercising a three-pool fallback chain.

Files & artifacts:
- Incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-03-10+-+Rate+Envelope+Handoff
- Grafana dash: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ab123/rate-limiter-ops
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12984
- Staging e2e: https://ci.redwood.ai/blue/organizations/jenkins/platform/detail/e2e/523

Rollout plan:
- PR merged to canary channel (runtime-1.20.2-canary) and deployed to 5% of traffic (canary window: 4hrs).
- If no regressions, ramp to 25% over 2 hours, then 100% in Dedicated and Private control planes.
- Post-rollout: keep augmented monitoring for 72 hours and run regression evals on a representative prompt set.

Open follow-ups (action items):
- Add a formal contract and test harness for epoch marker compatibility between proxy <-> admission-controller (ENG-91300).
- Review fallback policy heuristics to avoid rapid oscillation under blended load (PM ticket assigned).
- Add customer-facing postmortem and update SLA credit process for transient handoff failures.

Notes: This ticket intentionally avoids touching token accounting codepaths; change is limited to admission-controller handoff reconciliation and proxy acknowledgement to reduce blast radius.
